label: PROMPT: long-term NSAID
title: NSAID used for more than three months
statement: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) (e.g. celecoxib, diclofenac, naproxen) should not be used long-term (greater than three months).

source.document: Cooper JA, et al. The development of the PROMPT criteria. BMC Health Serv Res 2014;14:484, Table 4
source.citation: Cooper JA, Ryan C, Smith SM, et al. The development of the PROMPT (PRescribing Optimally in Middle-aged People's Treatments) criteria. BMC Health Serv Res 2014;14:484
source.credit: Cooper JA, Ryan C, Smith SM, et al. The development of the PROMPT (PRescribing Optimally in Middle-aged People's Treatments) criteria. BMC Health Serv Res 2014;14:484

plain_summary: Anti-inflammatory pain medicines (NSAIDs) used for months raise the risk of stomach bleeding, kidney damage, high blood pressure and heart problems.

medicine_groups.name: Systemic NSAIDs

ibuprofen: Advil Childrens Pain and Fever 2 to 7 Years
Advil Childrens Pain and Fever 7 to 12 Years
Advil Childrens Pain and Fever Relief 2 to 12 Years
Advil Infants Pain and Fever Relief 3 Months to 2 Years
Nurofen for Children 3 Months to 5 Years

medicine_groups.note: Oral NSAIDs count. Count diclofenac or indometacin suppositories and intramuscular ketorolac. If another rectal or injectable product appears, leave the match uncertain and ask the pharmacist to identify the preparation. Skin gels, creams and eye drops do not count, for example Orudis gel or Voltaren Emulgel. Aspirin is not in this group. Nurofen Plus and Panafen Plus are ibuprofen with codeine. Nuromol and Maxigesic are ibuprofen with paracetamol. Arthrotec is diclofenac with misoprostol. Vimovo is naproxen with esomeprazole. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

rule_for_models: For patients aged 45 through 64 during treatment (confirm age if unknown), suspect one course of Group A systemic NSAIDs lasting more than three calendar months using these checks: divide each quantity by the number taken daily, count from the first dose through the last dose covered including switches within the course, exclude skin gels, creams, eye drops and documented separate courses, check for an interruption if about 30 days or more are uncovered after a supply runs out, and report uncertain duration if continuity is unclear. When repeated supplies span more than three calendar months but directions give no fixed daily dose, report only a possible finding if one continuous course is plausible. Ask how much was taken each day, on which days, and whether there were breaks.
cannot_be_seen: Why the NSAID was prescribed, how often it is really taken, NSAIDs bought without a prescription, kidney function, blood pressure and stomach history.
ask_the_gp: Whether the NSAID is still needed, and whether a safer pain plan is possible.
